note: Continued past the earlier 'leader-gap-unexplained' checkpoint at the user's explicit request. Fresh pass (046-061) found: the champion's long-standing 'water is 10x short' comment is wrong (real water sits at 0.8-1.0); every unlock level is genuinely maxed including Speed and Fertilizer (052, live unlock() attempts); tighter drone packing and every distance-aware reroll/accept variant tried (051, 053-055, 058-061 -- eight variants total) measured worse than or tied the simple champion, never better -- a consistent signal, not noise. A clean growth-floor re-measurement (056) found 415 ticks at water~1 (not ~608-724 as the wiki's raw seconds implied), putting the zero-servicing floor at ~815 ticks/harvest, inside the #2-10 cluster's implied ~750-856 band. Tick-budget model (given move/plant/harvest=200 each): total = 400 (own handling) + max(S, 415); solving the reroll-only recurrence at the real per-draw hit rate (~1/3) gives S's asymptote at ~800 -- ABOVE the growth floor, meaning servicing, not growth, is what 057 is bound by, and no accept-policy variant found a way past that asymptote. The one real, adopted win: full memory-matched reroll-before-walk (any type), REROLL_LIMIT=5, water 0.999 -- 02:42.421, Global Rank #111 (was 02:47.682, #130/131); REROLL_LIMIT=5 is confirmed the local optimum (3 and 10 both worse, 058/059). WEB RESEARCH (2026-08-17, user's suggestion): the game's Dec 4 2025 'Leaderboard Rebalance' patch reset all boards specifically because 'old times are no longer correct' after three exploit fixes in the same update -- shared memory bugs between drones (which we independently confirmed structurally closed, exp-050), RNG made 'harder to break' (not 'unbreakable'), and a zero-tick computation exploit via dynamic-module function calls. This strongly explains #1's implied ~409-466 ticks/harvest budget sitting BELOW even our zero-servicing floor (815) as a residual exploit, not a design gap -- #2-10's tight cluster is the honest current-mechanics ceiling and remains the real target. EXPLOIT-CANDIDATE CHECK (062, 2026-08-17): since boards were reset, current #1 must be a post-patch submission -- the user correctly pointed out a residual exploit should in principle be replicable now too. Checked two cheap candidates: direct Hay tradeability (not a real mechanism -- get_cost() only accepts Entity/Unlock, no trade()/sell()/buy() exists in the API at all) and a module-function-call tick-cost gap mirroring the patched 'free function calls in dynamic modules' exploit (none found -- Common.py function calls cost exactly their real body work, and indirect-via-variable costs exactly +1 tick over direct, matching Operation-Costs.md precisely, for both local and imported-module functions). Both closed with no champion change. RNG-SEED MECHANISM (063, 2026-08-17): decompiled Core.dll (Mono IL, static read-only inspection) and confirmed leaderboard_run() hardcodes seed=-1 at the call site itself, forcing Mono's parameterless System.Random() -- seeded from Environment.TickCount (system uptime), not wall-clock date/time. Every other RNG stream (growth, maze, companion draws) cascades from that one root value. A theoretical exploit sketch (offline seed search via simulate(), invert seed to TickCount, time the leaderboard_run() trigger) was NOT attempted -- unverified sub-ms timing through several jittery layers, and even a perfect hit would only control one of a 2-hour session's 100+ averaged repeats (the leaderboard's 'average over 2 hours' scoring rule caps the realistic benefit at ~1% or less). Closed on practical grounds and the standing concern about manipulating a shared public leaderboard; full writeup docs/RNG-Seed-Mechanism.md. SEED-LUCK-VS-GROWTH-FLOOR (064, 2026-08-17): user asked whether a forced-favorable seed (e.g. by controlling system uptime) could explain #1's budget -- tested directly by sweeping simulate()'s seed parameter across 24 values and measuring 056's isolated growth-time floor at each (sandboxed, never touched the live leaderboard). 20/24 seeds landed on the same floor value, 4/24 landed on exactly double it (one whole extra growth cycle) -- NO seed went below the floor. RNG luck only ever costs a cycle, never saves one -- the seed-timing exploit has nothing to exploit even in the most generous reading, on top of 063's own practicality problems. HARVEST-RACE-DUPLICATION-CHECK (065, 2026-08-17): last open brainstorm lead -- could the known drone-concurrency race (050) be provoked to duplicate a harvest rather than just fail cheaply? Tested directly: two drones spawned on the same tile racing to harvest() the same ripe plant. Both executed harvest() and each locally observed a 512 gain, but the true final total was before+512, not before+1024 -- only one harvest ever lands, the loser's call is a silent no-op. Confirms 046/047's plant-side finding generalizes: the race resolves cleanly, never duplicates. This closes the exploit-hunt in full -- all four brainstormed leads (Hay tradeability, module-call cost gap, RNG-seed timing/luck, harvest-race duplication) came back empty. #1's implied budget remains unexplained by anything found in this investigation, consistent with it reflecting a residual/historical mechanic the Dec 2025 patch closed. SCOPE NOTE: the Grass-auto-regrow finding below is Hay-specific, not general -- checked Cactus.md, Sunflowers.md, Pumpkins.md, Trees.md/Tree.md, and Carrots.md for the same 'grows automatically' language Grass.md has; none of them have it (Carrots.md explicitly describes a real till/plant/harvest cycle instead). This correction does not carry over to other leaderboard categories without checking each one's own entity page first. CORRECTION (066, 2026-08-17): the '400-tick own-handling floor' asserted throughout every note above (046-065) is WRONG. User pushback, tested directly: Grass.md says outright 'Grass grows automatically on grassland' -- harvest() never leaves the tile empty, get_companion() rerolls fresh every single cycle with no plant() call, and the champion's instructions() call after harvest() is a guarded plant() whose guard always skips (entity_type never leaves Grass) -- measured at 7 ticks, not 200, in 6/6 cycles. Real own-handling cost: harvest (200) + instructions (7) = ~207, not 400. This halves the reroll cost R used in every servicing-cost estimate since 046: S = R(1-p)/p drops from ~800 to ~414, and the zero-servicing floor (own-handling + 415 growth) drops from ~815 to ~622 -- well BELOW the #2-10 cluster's ~750-856 band, not barely inside it. This does NOT overturn 051/053-055/058-061's specific measured results (real game runs, unaffected by a wrong model) but DOES overturn the narrative built on them ('057 is at the true optimum, further tuning can't help, the paradigm is servicing-bound') -- that reasoning used the wrong number throughout. REROLL-PATTERN VALIDATION (067) confirmed the 207-tick number in the champion's exact usage (no ripeness check) -- no correction needed. REAL-TICKS-PER-HARVEST MEASUREMENT (068, 2026-08-17) then corrected the premature conclusion drawn from 066: directly measured the unmodified champion, single drone, 900 cycles (matching a real drone's ~871/run), windowed every 150. Memory saturates by cycle 300 (~23-24 of ~25 reachable positions) and never grows further, so cycles 300-900 ARE steady state -- and steady-state ticks/harvest plateaus at ~1070-1220, nowhere near the corrected 622 floor or even the old 815 one. Cause: 17.2% of cycles exhaust all 5 rerolls with no memory hit even at full maturity (vs ~8.8% a naive independent-draw model at p=1/3 predicts) and fall through to a real walk (200-1200 ticks) next cycle -- a structural tax the operation-cost floor treated as avoidable. 066/067's operation costs (207, not 400) are still correct and stand; the 'real headroom, worth reopening' conclusion drawn from them does not and is retracted. If there is a real lever left, per queue.md's 069, it's reducing the exhaustion tail's walk-fallback cost specifically (e.g. remembering the cheapest seen-but-unmatched option across the reroll chase, not just retuning REROLL_LIMIT, which 058/059 already correctly bracketed under these same true costs) -- not yet implemented or tested. 062-065's exploit-hunt closure is unaffected by any of this and stands on its own. #1's implied budget still remains unexplained by anything found so far.
